results.title: Silence Removal Software: Windows, Mac, Linux (2026) | VoxCut
results.content:
## Which silence removers run on Windows, Mac and Linux?

 Audacity: free and open source, available on Windows, Mac and Linux; its Truncate Silence effect shortens pauses. See the Audacity site.
 Adobe Audition: a professional audio editor for Windows and Mac, sold on subscription.
 Descript: an editor where you cut by editing the transcript; it is cloud-based and has desktop apps. See VoxCut vs Descript.
 TimeBolt: a local-first video editor for Mac and Windows, covered in the best TimeBolt alternatives.
 Auto-Editor: a free command-line tool with no graphical interface, available for Windows, Mac and Linux.
 VoxCut: a desktop app for Windows and Linux, plus an Android app, processing everything locally on your device. [...] A word on limits, since they decide whether a free tool is enough. The free version of VoxCut handles files up to 10 minutes and 500 MB, with 3 exports per day. That is fine to test it on a real recording; for full episodes or batches, you need the Pro version. For long files, see removing silence from large audio files.

## What if you are on Linux?

Linux has fewer polished options. Audacity and Auto-Editor both run there, and VoxCut offers a Linux build as an AppImage and an archive. Browser tools are the fallback for one-off jobs. If you prefer a graphical interface over a terminal, an Auto-Editor alternative without the command line explains where a GUI helps and where Auto-Editor remains the better choice.

## How should you choose, whatever your system? [...] Audacity is the one to try first: it costs nothing, runs entirely on your computer, and its Truncate Silence effect covers the basic need. The price is hands-on work, since you set the threshold and check the result yourself, one file at a time.

## What if you are on Windows?

Windows has the widest choice. Beyond the cross-platform tools above, Windows users can run VoxCut, built for one job: detecting and removing silence quickly on large files, with a waveform preview and an adjustable threshold. Pick it if silence removal is the task you repeat every week and you do not want a subscription; choose a bigger editor if you also need transcript editing or multitrack mixing.
